You set five goals in January. You got through one and a half, then lay on the floor for a week, then decided the problem was your discipline.

So you added pressure. Five a.m. wake-ups. A tracker. A written promise to yourself with a date on it. Three days of that and the collapse is deeper than the first one.

Zhuangzi starts his third chapter with a line that has been carved on desks for two thousand years. My life has a limit. Knowledge has none. To chase the unlimited with the limited is a dangerous business.

It's usually quoted as career advice, meaning read less or choose a field. I read it as arithmetic.

You have one day's worth of energy. You spent the morning repaying a debt you took out three months ago, and the afternoon negotiating with a list that has no end. By seven in the evening the account is overdrawn, and then you call yourself lazy.

Exhaustion of this kind rarely begins in the body. It begins in a bad sum.

MOJOWAY has no interest in handing you more targets. It's a place to get honest about the size of the day you actually have, and that honesty is where growth stops being a fantasy.

Full piece: https://mojowaylife.com/stories/13-five-goals-one-collapse.html
